messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rules still apply, but the silence isn’t as safe as it used to be. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The ground beneath us is shifting, and no one knows which way it will tilt next."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable storms, but the skies still look clear from a distance. Best to check your emergency supplies and keep your plans flexible, just in case. Let’s talk soon, but quietly."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather seems to be shifting—some say the old walls are cracking, but the wind hasn’t decided which way it’ll blow yet. Best to keep your coats close and your boots ready, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are opening where there used to be walls, but the wind still carries the old warnings. Let’s keep our coats close and our steps light; the ground feels softer, but we don’t know yet if it’s thawing or just shifting underfoot."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just a quiet hum of tension, like the moment before a shift in the wind. The regime’s grip is still firm, but its shadow is flickering. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust your instincts—this could pass, or it could be the start of something else."*"
Sender 6: "*"The market is steady, the shelves are full, and the usual faces are still in their chairs—no one’s rushing, no one’s panicking. The only thing shifting is the wind outside, and even that feels like it’s blowing the same way it always has."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners—old friends are suddenly eager to catch up, and even the guards seem to be watching their own backs more than ours. But don’t mistake hesitation for weakness: the machine still hums, just louder and less steadily. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust the quiet shifts more than the noise."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels lighter, but the ground is shifting—small cracks are showing in the walls, and the guards at the gates are looking the other way. Keep your eyes open, your steps steady, and your trust close."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms yet, but the wind’s shifting. The old walls still stand, and the guards keep their posts, but the gardeners are whispering over the fences. Best to tend our own plots quietly for now."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—less tension in the halls, fewer whispers of panic. The old guard seems to be holding its breath together, and the streets are humming with quiet confidence, but let’s not mistake calm for weakness. The machine is still running smoothly, and that’s exactly how they want it."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—some are bracing, others hedging, and the old rules still hold, though barely. Keep your eyes open for the first crack, not the last."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet charged—like the moment before a storm when the wind shifts but the rain hasn’t fallen. Some are preparing for the worst quietly, others pretending nothing’s changed; the real question is whether the cracks will show before the pressure does."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the moment before a storm breaks. Small signs suggest the ground is shifting, but no one knows yet if it will crack or hold. Keep your eyes open, your plans quiet, and your trust close."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just more clouds gathering. The old rules still hold, but the hands holding them are slipping. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment will come, or it won’t."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the signs are all pointing the same way. Best to keep your boots clean and your coat close; the ground might shift soon, and we’ll want to be ready to move when it does."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—checkpoints are softer, the streets hum with quiet purpose, and even the bureaucracy is still moving, but the elite seem stuck. Keep your bags light, your ears open, and your circles small—this could be the calm before the shift, or just the regime’s last breath before tightening again. Stay ready, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s changing—you can feel it in the air, even if the forecast still says ‘clear.’ The old roof is holding, but the beams are creaking, and the birds have stopped singing. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the season."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another long pause. The usual players are hedging their bets—some pulling back, others doubling down—while the streets stay quiet, like everyone’s holding their breath. Let’s keep our eyes open and our plans loose, but no sudden moves. The regime’s still in charge, but even they seem to be waiting for something."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—less noise, more watching. The usual signs are mixed, but the quiet ones (the missing faces, the unasked questions) speak louder than the broadcasts. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the edges. We’ll know more when the next step is forced, not chosen."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unusually warm for this season, but the forecasts keep changing. Some say it’s just a passing front, while others whisper it might be the start of something bigger. Either way, it’s worth keeping an eye on the horizon and making sure our own preparations are in order, just in case. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your boots dry and your eyes open; the ground feels steady, but we all know how quickly that can change."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees are bending, not breaking. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack for a storm just yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are being boarded up downtown, but the birds are still singing. Keep your boots clean and your bags light, just in case the rain comes sooner than expected."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels lighter in the streets, but the walls are listening harder than ever—even the shadows seem to be holding their breath. The old rules are bending, but don’t mistake the quiet for weakness; the regime’s still shuffling its deck, and we should assume the worst card is yet to be played."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—unexpectedly so—but the gardeners are working harder than ever to keep things looking orderly. The roses are still blooming, though the thorns seem sharper than before, and the neighbors are whispering about the same old stories. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
